two-ledgers.title: A debit with no credit
two-ledgers.caption: Time runs down the page. The debit was written; the deploy landed before the credit, so €50,000 left the treasury ledger and reached no other.

sum-over.title: SumOver, unwound
sum-over.caption: Each call takes one loan out and calls itself on the rest, until the set is empty. Then the sums come back up: 0, then 30,000, then 80,000.

conservation.title: Where the money is, row by row
conservation.caption: The same two tables as bars. A dip that the next write fills is normal; after the crash, €50,000 stays missing in every row, and the run ends €50,000 short.

crash-window.title: Two orders, two wrong totals
crash-window.caption: The crash lands in the gap between two writes either way. Debit first leaves the books €50,000 short; credit first leaves them €50,000 over, and the bakery’s account at €100,000.

two-phase.title: Prepared, then stranded
two-phase.caption: Two-phase commit, if the loan ledger could take part (it cannot: its HTTP API does not speak the protocol). After both say yes, neither may decide alone. If the coordinator crashes before commit, both wait with their locks held.

outbox.title: The debit and the debt, together
outbox.caption: One transaction writes the debit and the outbox row together. The relay then does three things in order: read the row, credit the loan ledger, delete the row.

at-least-once.title: Delivered twice, credited once
at-least-once.caption: The same steps and the same crash, twice. The relay delivers row 4471 twice either way; only the key decides whether the bakery’s account shows it twice.
